text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "Each weight is the ratio of a state's probability under the current potential θ to its probability under the reference potential θ̂, normalized over all N states: wi = [pθ(Si)/pθ̂(Si)] / Σj [pθ(Sj)/pθ̂(Sj)] [W3168247670#005]. Assuming a canonical ensemble, state probabilities are Boltzmann, pθ(Si) ~ exp(−βH(Si)), where H is the sum of potential and kinetic energy and β = 1/(kB T) [W3168247670#005]. Substituting this into the ratio makes the kinetic energy cancel, so wi = exp(−β(Uθ(Si) − Uθ̂(Si))) / Σj exp(−β(Uθ(Sj) − Uθ̂(Sj))) [W3168247670#005]. The passage states that the kinetic energy cancels but does not spell out the algebra. Since the kinetic-energy term is the same in the numerator and denominator of each ratio, it appears to drop out, but that reasoning is my inference rather than something the passage says. When θ = θ̂, wi = 1/N [W3168247670#005]."}
